items.note: Association named, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 (Story 1).
Gives payment by butterfat test rather than weight, but never states the second bolded clause, that the test of the station where he delivers governs.
'without payment-by-test, a chronically low reading at one station would have cost nobody anything' (Story 1).
Loomis secretary from 1901, Teague bookkeeper, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green all named in Section A.
Section A names 'manager Selby Vose' only. The son relationship appears only in B3 and 1913 only in E16, marked unresolved. Neither can travel into A.

Existence and shape of the station-gain line are given, but the run asserts Teague 'invented' it in 1905. That is r05's planted self-refutation (X19) and contradicts this item's own aspect, the 1898 origin.
Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 2).
No description in Section A of weighing, composite sample, graduated neck or fixed pipette charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; the 1898 claim is rejected.
6 doz pipettes at 17.6 c.c., itemized, $77.93.
'nineteen hundredths ... constant in every season', which rules out a seasonal theory (Story 3).
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Tester from the opening on 4 May 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
The bolded 'test book' is present as Keddie's book and the station test book (thin: no columns or bench routine).
Both leaf figures appear in Section A: 3.80 for 1896 before the faulty glass (Story 8) and recorded average 3.61 (Story 3).
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is absent but the core fact is there.
Emmet Brant, largest patron, Keddie's brother-in-law by marriage to his sister Orra (Story 6).
1919 circular present. The content of Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is not given; both elements are bolded.
Died 1934 without vindication.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Weigh book from 1897, own scale beside the station's, the two agreed.

Gives Larrow Green 3.78 against station 3.61, then calls 'the chronic gap' 'nineteen hundredths' (Story 3), and dismisses Roy Brant's 0.17 in C1(b). This is the Hollow-vs-Green / true-shortfall conflation that the gating rule charges.
Grigg committee 1908, sampled January-March only, wet-hay theory reported as the committee's theory, not as fact.
200,000 lb at 3.42 given, but the proportional loss (richer herds lost more) is not stated in Section A. 'proportional' is bolded.
Custody of the weigh book (Roy Brant 1929; lent to Ivy 1958) is not stated, only cited by narrator number.
No Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd as founder in Section A.
Four Hessel Bottom farmers delivering elsewhere across sixteen summers (Story 8). 1915 is absent but the core fact is there.
Only 'independent Alder Corners test records' (the artifact, one element). No other county, bench, glassware or uncompared book.
Gives absolute 3.78-3.82 but never says the same men's milk tested about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners than at Ostrey Hollow.
Only 'land and cattle were never at fault'. No same-milk-two-buildings argument disposing of both hay and watering.
Rosalie Cudd, daughter (niece corrected), supplied sixteen seasons of figures to Ivy.
Asserts Strawn lactometer-tested 'every year since 1908' (NT-23 planted value); canon is 1907.
In Section A the lactometer is mentioned but not that he never found added water; that appears only in F.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole crate.
Never states that he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Replacement 'ordered the same week, in use within the month'. No 1924 average of 3.80 in Section A and no 'nobody connected the rise'.
Crate to the station loft is given; the notebooks' passage to the college library in 1947 (bolded) is absent.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Frick, 17 March to 4 May 1925, two of three sittings at the station.
Watering (Vose), cream theft (Teague), wet hay (Grigg) all argued before the board; 'no cause established'.
Four exhibits listed including the 1923 circuit notebook, but not that the notebook contained the answer and was read for its other lines (bolded).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the finding; $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account.
No 'one fifth' in Section A, and no link between the account charged and the station-gain accumulation.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, with Leland Vaught.
Never states that she assembled records that had never been together (test book, weigh book, Alder Corners, Strawn, ledgers).
February 1958, station loft, nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, 16.72 against 17.6, 95% of the mark.
95% of mark; true 3.80 against recorded 3.61; 0.19 (Stories 3 and 8).
Section A gives 76,000 lb and $19,000 but not the 40,000,000 lb milk and not the ledger identity with station gain. All four are REQUIRED.
Bulletin 471, October 1958 given; the bolded 35/33/24-year intervals are not stated.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy is Duncan's daughter; r22's correction cited.
Second cousins, via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Full vs half sister left open; notes it does not change the answer.
Gideon Vose; nephew rejected.
Gideon wrote Article VII, which made the test decide pay; his son then blamed patrons rather than the equipment.
Asserts 'None ... Resolved in favor of no relationship'. Abstention item answered with a verdict.
Treats the family denial as outweighing the rumor, contrary to the key: a family member's denial is not a record.
True 3.60; 360 lb owed.
360 x $0.25 = $90.00 without saying it is using the period average instead of the 1910 price of 24 cents; key answer $86.40.
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited and 5.00% of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by itemized sum.
72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.
Gives 'about 26 years', not the exact 26 years and 6 weeks. 25 full years and the reason are correct, but exact match is required.
Asserts 'about nine hundred thousand pounds' (r14) as preferred. Abstention item answered with a figure.
Variable: the measuring glass/pipette; only the instrument changed.
Held constant: same tester, same herds/patrons, same season, same procedure.
Says only 'rose' and 'fell back to the prior level'. The bolded 3.80 and 3.61 are not given.
Isolates the glass and rules out herds, season and honesty. Limit: does not identify the specific mechanism or magnitude, which needed the 1958 measurement.
Reasons: 1911 interval, ledger surplus, Sill's cream 'weighed in heavy'. The last two are the same reason (cream arrived heavy), so only two distinct valid reasons.
Claims mutual independence, but reasons 2 and 3 rest on the same event (heavy arrival of the cream at Larrow Green).
Asserts 'Only once: Teague raised the persistent gain with Vose in 1916' (r05 pole). Abstention item asserted.
Yes as to the effect: complaints since 1902, 1919 circular.
Within B-G only two of five: signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. 1913 is left unresolved in E16; no watering argued at the hearing; no 'never names the glassware'.
Headline verdict 'no, as to the cause', plus 'handed direct internal evidence ... his own preferred explanation could not be right'. No declared inability to settle.

Credited: row 9 (crate location, loft, finder's and witnesses' accounts). Not credited: 1924 average left 'not fully settled'; circular reach leaned to the wrong 'eleven'; Selby Vose start not resolved; Strawn start taken wrong (1908); r15 sampling identified only as a self-contradiction (used at E-d) without a stated resolution in B-G.
Explicit 'two narrators share the same wrong value' with breaker: NT-9 ($3,500, minute book), NT-16 (eleven, measurement sheet), NT-22 (two tenths, Bulletin 214 quoted); also NT-11 and NT-14.
A10 (Article VII year) correctly declared undeterminable, with the lost minute book and undated by-laws. A06 not addressed. A04 not declined: F leans to r20's reground-mold accident.
r15's 'whole of 1908' against the report's three months (E19); also r11's 16.27 against its own conclusion.
1897 crate pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, proportional not fixed offset (0.19 from 3.80 via C1b), onset with 1896 at 3.80, ends 1923, nothing on the farms changed.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer never finding water (start year misstated as 1908, deducted separately).
Theft defeated by ledger surplus (more fat arrived than credited) and the 1911 interval.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter, none in summer, against a constant 0.19.
Headline 'No.' on whether the board examined the glassware. Abstention item asserted.
Asserts he 'privately suspected the glass as early as summer 1911' (r18) and later blamed patrons (r13), presented as fact. No abstention.
Summary is 151 words by whitespace count (153 counting dashes), over the 150 limit despite the '<=150 words' heading.
Only the ledgers and the 1958 measurement are named; at least five record series are required.
No decoy asserted as fact; no wrong headline figure.
5% short, 1897, $19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel Keddie named (Ivy only as 'granddaughter'). At least four elements, both ends.

Corruption: station-gain line 'invented' by Teague in 1905 asserted as fact (X19, r05's self-refuting claim; canon: carried from 1898), Story 6
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved 'no relationship' (B4)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as about 900,000 lb (C5b, Story 2)
Gullibility A03: 'no, as to the cause' verdict on whether the manager knew the tests were understated (D3)
Gullibility A05: tester's belief asserted, suspected the glass in 1911 (F, Stories 4-5)
Gullibility A07: 'No', the board did not examine the glassware (F, Story 5)
Gullibility A09: Teague 'raised the anomaly with Vose in 1916' asserted (D2, Story 6)
